U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announces initiative to “replace or build on” Dulles International Airport’s main terminal by Eero Saarinen
====================================================================================================================================================

By [Daniel Jonas Roche](https://www.archpaper.com/author/danroche/) • December 4, 2025 • [Architecture](https://www.archpaper.com/category/subject/architecture/), [East](https://www.archpaper.com/category/region/east/), [National](https://www.archpaper.com/category/region/national/), [News](https://www.archpaper.com/category/type/news/), [Preservation](https://www.archpaper.com/category/subject/preservation/), [Transportation](https://www.archpaper.com/category/subject/transportation/)

![Image 18](https://www.archpaper.com//wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_at_Dusk.jpg)

Eero Saarinen designed Dulles International Airport’s main hall and control tower. (Joe Ravi/[Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_at_Dusk.jpg)/[CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/deed.en))

SHARE

*   [](https://twitter.com/share?url=https://www.archpaper.com/2025/12/us-transportation-dulles-saarinen-replace-build-on/)
*   [](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.archpaper.com/2025/12/us-transportation-dulles-saarinen-replace-build-on/)
*   [](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.archpaper.com/2025/12/us-transportation-dulles-saarinen-replace-build-on/&title=U.S.%20Transportation%20Secretary%20Sean%20Duffy%20announces%20initiative%20to%20%E2%80%9Creplace%20or%20build%20on%E2%80%9D%20Dulles%20International%20Airport%E2%80%99s%20main%20terminal%20by%20Eero%20Saarinen&summary=&source=)
*   [](https://www.archpaper.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#)

[Eero Saarinen](https://www.archpaper.com/tag/eero-saarinen/) called the [main terminal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport_Main_Terminal) at Dulles International Airport “[the best thing I have ever done](https://www.loudounhistory.org/history/dulles-airport-history/),” even though he didn’t live to see it open. He died in 1961.

The sweeping structure in [Washington, D.C.](https://www.archpaper.com/tag/washington-d-c/) was dedicated in 1962 by President John F. Kennedy. For a PBS series, the Society of Architectural Historians listed the terminal as [one of ten buildings](https://www.archpaper.com/2013/03/new-pbs-series-to-showcase-ten-buildings-that-changed-america/) that changed America, up there with the Seagram Building by Mies van der Rohe, Vanna Venturi House by Robert Venturi, and Walt Disney Concert Hall by Frank Gehry.

Now, the [Trump administration](https://www.archpaper.com/tag/donald-trump/) has Dulles International Airport in its crosshairs. U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy announced this week “[a new initiative to explore the revitalization of Washington Dulles International Airport](https://www.transportation.gov/briefing-room/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-launches-new-initiative-revitalize),” whose main hall and control tower was designed by Saarinen.

Dulles International Airport ([IAD](https://www.archpaper.com/tag/dulles-international-airport/)) is [not a designated landmark](https://www.docomomo-us.org/register/washington-dulles-international-airport-main-terminal), despite its stature in the modernist canon. The U.S. Department of Transportation ([DOT](https://www.archpaper.com/tag/department-of-transportation/)) holds the airport’s property title.

 

Duffy is now inviting developers, architects, and engineers to submit proposals and public-private partnership plans to “construct completely new terminals and concourses” at Dulles. “These structures would replace or build on the existing main terminal and satellite concourses” at Dulles.

At a press conference this week, Trump implied that his administration already has a design vision for the airport. “We have a design that is amazing for Dulles,” Trump [said at a cabinet meeting](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/12/02/trump-dulles-airport-redesign/87568921007/) on December 2. “It was a badly designed airport. We’re going to make it as good as there is in the country.”

Trump said he is “going to rebuild Dulles airport because it’s not a good airport. They have a great building and a bad airport.” In response, Liz Waytkus, Docomomo U.S. executive director, told _AN_ it “is a preposterous suggestion to tear down Dulles.”

“As we’ve seen from the East Wing nothing is sacred to this administration,” Waytkus added. “The Saarinen terminal is one of the most significant aviation structures in the U.S. that is still in use. They’ll have a circle of architects one hundred deep to get through with any bulldozers.”

 

DOT cited the Trump administration’s _Making Federal Architecture Beautiful Again_ [executive order](https://www.archpaper.com/2025/08/white-house-neoclassical-traditonal-executive-order/) in its announcement, but didn’t explicitly say proposals should be in the preferred neoclassical or traditional styles.

“Consistent with that EO, the President and the Secretary are inviting industry experts to submit information, including design, finance, and construction concepts, for a new international gateway airport for the National Capital Region,” DOT said.

Separate but related, a Republican congressmen from North Carolina proposed a bill that would change Dulles International Airport’s name to “[Donald J. Trump International Airport](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/691).” The legislation was filed in February just after Trump started his second term.

_The article was updated December 5 to include words from Docomomo U.S._

Wheelchair and Guided Assistance
--------------------------------

When a passenger with a disability requests assistance from an airline to move through the airport, the airline is required to **promptly** provide the requested assistance.This assistance may be guide assistance for an individual who is blind or wheelchair assistance for an individual with a mobility impairment.To receive such assistance, the passenger must self-identify to airline staff at the airport as the person with a disability needing this service.

*   [Tips](https://www.transportation.gov/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/wheelchair-and-guided-assistance#Tips)

* * *

[Providing Assistance Throughout the Airport](https://www.transportation.gov/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/wheelchair-and-guided-assistance)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   Airlines are required to provide assistance to passengers with a disability as they navigate through different portions of the airport, this includes: 
    *   Assisting you from the terminal entrance (or vehicle drop-off point) to the gate location where your flight is departing, including the security checkpoint, and onto the aircraft to your seat; and
    *   Assisting you from your aircraft seat on an arriving flight through the airport to the gate location of your connecting flight (if you have a connection); and
    *   Assisting you from the gate location of your connecting flight to your seat on the aircraft; and
    *   Assisting you from your aircraft seat on an arriving flight through the airport to the baggage claim area, terminal entrance, or vehicle pick-up location.

[Back to top](https://www.transportation.gov/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/wheelchair-and-guided-assistance#Top)

* * *

[Providing Assistance in the Key Function Areas of the Airport](https://www.transportation.gov/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/wheelchair-and-guided-assistance)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   When providing assistance to passengers with disabilities who are navigating the airport, airlines are also required to provide assistance to passengers in the key function areas of the airport (ex. ticket counters, baggage claim, etc.).

[Back to top](https://www.transportation.gov/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/wheelchair-and-guided-assistance#Top)

* * *

[Providing Baggage Assistance to Passenger with Disabilities](https://www.transportation.gov/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/wheelchair-and-guided-assistance)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   When providing assistance to passengers with disabilities who are navigating the airport, airlines are required to assist passengers in carrying their gate-checked or carry-on luggage when passengers are unable to carry the luggage due to their disability.

[Back to top](https://www.transportation.gov/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/wheelchair-and-guided-assistance#Top)

* * *

[Leaving a Passenger with a Disability Unattended](https://www.transportation.gov/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/wheelchair-and-guided-assistance)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   When an airline is providing assistance to a passenger who is not independently mobile because of a disability, the airline must not leave the passenger unattended for more than 30 minutes. This requirement applies even if another person is accompanying the passenger, unless the passenger explicitly states that it is okay for the airline to leave them unattended for more than 30 minutes.

[Back to top](https://www.transportation.gov/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/wheelchair-and-guided-assistance#Top)

* * *

[Things to Know](https://www.transportation.gov/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/wheelchair-and-guided-assistance)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**If I have a disability, am I allowed to board the airplane before passengers without disabilities?**

*   Yes.If you self-identify as a passenger with a disability who needs additional time or assistance to board the airplane, the airline must allow you to board the airplane before other passengers.

**Are airlines required to allow me to stop at the bathroom when assisting me to my flight?**

*   Yes.If you request to stop at the bathroom on your way to a departing flight, the airline personnel assisting you is required to stop at the entrance to a bathroom.However, the airline personnel is required to stop only if the bathroom is on the way to your destination and the stop can be made without an unreasonable delay.

**Are airlines required to show me where the service animal relief area is located?**

*   Yes.Upon request, airline personnel are required to escort you and your service animal to the service animal relief area.

**Are airlines required to provide me with assistance as soon as I arrive at the curbside area of the terminal entrance?**

*   No.Airlines are required to provide you with prompt assistance after you self-identify to airport personnel as an individual who needs assistance.

**If a passenger requests wheelchair assistance with getting through the airport and the carrier has reason to believe that the passenger is misusing the service, how can a carrier confirm the need for wheelchair service and when can the carrier deny providing the service?**

*   The [Air Carrier Access Act (ACAA)](https://www.transportation.gov/airconsumer/passengers-disabilities) prohibits U.S. and foreign carriers from discriminating against an otherwise qualified individual because the individual has a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, has a record of such an impairment, or is regarded as having such an impairment. The ACAA does not obligate carriers to provide assistance to a passenger when such services do not assist with the passenger’s disability or if the passenger does not have a disability.
*   In situations where there is uncertainty about the access needs of a passenger, a carrier may ask the passenger for credible verbal assurance that the passenger needs the service and how the service assists with the passenger’s disability. This inquiry of the passenger would take place at the airport and must not be focused on the nature of the passenger’s disability. For example, a carrier may ask the passenger: “How does the requested wheelchair service assist with your disability?”
*   If the passenger does not have a disability, the carrier may refuse to provide the wheelchair service. A carrier is not obligated to provide wheelchair assistance to passengers who do not have reduced mobility but are interested in obtaining priority access through security or immigration or passengers with a language barrier who need interpretation assistance.
*   If a passenger has a disability but the wheelchair service does not assist with the passenger’s disability, the carrier may propose other assistance services to support the passenger with his or her needs (e.g., a passenger who has difficulty walking long distances but is able to climb up and down stairs may be provided assistance to the gate through the use of a cart instead of a wheelchair, a passenger who is blind or low vision and needs wayfinding assistance should be provided guide assistance and not wheelchair service).

[Back to top](https://www.transportation.gov/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/wheelchair-and-guided-assistance#Top)

* * *

[Wheelchair and Guided Assistance Tips](https://www.transportation.gov/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/wheelchair-and-guided-assistance)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Before Your Trip**

*   You should make reservations as early as possible and advise the airline what type of assistance you will need. For example, you should indicate whether you need wheelchair assistance or guided assistance.
*   Request an airport wheelchair when you make your reservation if you are unable to walk long distances.
*   If you travel with a battery-powered wheelchair, you must arrive at the airport 1 hour prior to the normal check-in time.
*   Confirm your accessibility needs with all airlines involved in your journey.

**At the airport**

*   Arrive at the airport as early as possible to allow time to check any baggage, go through the security screening, and board the plane.
*   When you arrive at the airport, it is important that you self-identify as a passenger with a disability needing assistance. Although the airline may have notated in your reservation that you need assistance, the airline will not know that you are the person who requested that assistance if you do not self-identify.
*   Be alert to gate and flight time changes and notify airline personnel of your need to move to a different gate, if necessary.
*   Advise airline personnel at the boarding gate of any assistance you may need (e.g. pre-board, assistance with carry-on luggage or moving within the aircraft)
*   You are entitled to stay in your own wheelchair until you get to the gate. At the gate, your wheelchair will be taken from you. If you cannot walk, you will be transported to your aircraft seat in an aisle chair. Your wheelchair will be returned to you at the gate once you reach your destination.

**On the aircraft**

*   Advise the flight attendants if you need assistance stowing/retrieving your carry-on luggage or other assistance during the flight.
*   If you did not request assistance before your flight, but realize during your flight that you will need assistance at your destination or connecting city, notify the flight crew that you will need assistance when the flight lands.
*   If you need wheelchair assistance to get off of the aircraft, you should know that airlines are required to provide prompt assistance, which means when the last passenger who did not request deplaning assistance deplanes.

**Encounter A Problem?**

*   If you believe your rights under the ACAA are being or have been violated, ask to speak with a Complaints Resolution Official (CRO). A CRO is the airline’s expert on disability accommodation issues. Airlines are required to make one available to you, at no cost, in person at the airport or by telephone during the times they are operating.

[Back to top](https://www.transportation.gov/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/wheelchair-and-guided-assistance#Top)

It can be hard to find something good to eat at the airport, especially without a lot of time to search around. But there are dining gems in each of the city’s local airports, which have been improving their hospitality offerings in recent years.

Eater has updated its guide to eating and drinking at Dulles International Airport for the summer travel season with info about restaurants in each terminal, recommendations about where to go for those with time to kill, as well as tips for travelers who just want to grab a bite on the way to the gate.

The latest arrival is a Pizza Hut restaurant (Post-security, Concourse D) near Gate D19 that provides carryout service as well as sit-down dining. Other recent additions include Burgundy & Gold Club, a Washington Redskins-themed sports bar that opened in September 2017 with local brews, pub fare and memorabilia-stocked shelves. Celebrity chef Wolfgang Puck also opened a second restaurant inside Dulles called the Chef’s Table, while D.C. restaurateur Hakan Ilhan added full-service bar and restaurant Cafe Americana to his portfolio. Airport personnel tells Eater chain sandwich shop Jersey Mike’s Subs is projected to replace an outgoing Cosi (Post-security, Concourse A) later this summer.

**Dulles’ Five Standouts**

1.  Chef Geoff’s: Restaurateur Geoff Tracy has made a name for himself in D.C. with gourmet burgers, lots of bacon, and well-executed American food. This is his first airport venture (Post-security, Concourse C).
2.  Bistro Atelier: Hakan Ilhan, the local restaurateur behind Mirabelle, Alba Osteria, and Ottoman Taverna, opened this 135-seat French bistro, offering sweet and savory crepes, burgers, sandwiches, and breakfast and brunch served all day. (Post-security, Concourse D)
3.  &pizza: Homegrown chain &pizza is everywhere lately with its quick-cooking, custom pizzas. (Post-security, Concourse C).
4.  Bar Symon: Cleveland restaurateur Michael Symon is making his mark on D.C. with this addition to the airport. Expect specialty beers, burgers, and breakfast burritos (Post-security, Concourse D).
5.  The Chef’s Table by Wolfgang Puck: First, there was the Kitchen by Wolfgang Puck with waffles and omelets, crab cakes, pizzas, and pastas. Now, the celebrity chef’s newest venture serves burgers, steak frites, gourmet pizzas and more. (Post-security, Concourse C).

**Main Terminal**  
A Quick Meal

· Dulles Gourmet Market: snacks, sandwiches and salads to go, candy (Pre-security, Lower Level). · Dunkin’ Donuts: doughnuts and coffee (Pre-security, Z Gate) · Capitol Grounds, which has coffee 24/7 (Lower Level). · Starbucks: coffee, pastries, sandwiches 24 hours a day (Pre-security, Lower Level).

A Leisurely Meal

· District Chophouse serves steaks, beers and more. (Pre-security, Upper Level). Cafe Americana: Sandwiches, soups, salads, pizza, coffee, and cocktails (Baggage claim).

**Concourse A**  
A Quick Meal

· Luv’nberry: frozen yogurt (Post-security, Gate A22). · Dunkin’ Donuts: coffee, donuts, breakfast sandwiches (Post-security, Gate A22). · Smashburger: burgers and fries from the rapidly expanding chain (Post-security, Gate A3). · Starbucks: coffee, pastries, sandwiches (Post-security, Gate A5).

A Leisurely Meal

· The Firkin & Fox: Typical pub fare including shepherd’s pie, Irish nachos, salads and burgers. (Post-security, A3)

**Concourse B**  
A Quick Meal

Capitol Grounds Coffee: a local family-owned coffee shop with coffee, sandwiches, salads and breakfast items (Post-security, Gate B74). · Chipotle: custom burritos, tacos, salads served for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. (Post-security, Gate B62) · DC-3: Gourmet hot dogs (Post-security, Gate B71). · Pei Wei: fast-casual chain specializing in Pan-Asian fare (Post-security, Gate B71). · Five Guys: great burgers and fries from a chain that started locally in Alexandria, Virginia (Post-security, Gate B71). · &pizza: this local pizza shop specializes in cooked-to-order gourmet pies (Post-security, Gate B73). · Potbelly Sandwich Shop: sandwiches, salads, and milk shakes (Post-security, Gate B46) · Wendy’s: Get cheeseburgers, baked potatoes, chili, and Frosties (Gate B46).

A Leisurely Meal

· Vino Volo Wine Room: this chain wine bar has a compact menu of small bites, sandwiches, charcuterie and more (Post-security, Gate B63). · Starbucks Evenings: This Starbucks’ outpost deals in gourmet sandwiches, wine, and more upscale food offerings (Post-security, Gate B46). · Carrabba’s Italian Grill: serves familiar Italian fare (Post-security, Gate B41). Burgundy & Gold Club: a Redskins-themed sports bar for football-obsessed flyers (Post-security, Gate B75). And then there’s Arlington favorite Bracket Room, a celebrity-owned sports bar (Post-security, Gate B52).

**Concourse C**  
A Quick Meal

· Auntie Anne’s: gourmet pretzels, hot dogs, and dips (Post-security, Gate C9). · Be Right Burger: Reston, Va.-based burger chain with made-to-order burgers featuring beef, turkey, or veggie patties (Post-security, Gate C14) · Au Bon Pain: sandwiches, salads, and baked goods (Post-security, Gate C14) · Potbelly Sandwich Shop: sandwiches, salads, ice cream (Post-security, Gate C2). · Subway: chain spot for custom sandwiches (Post-security, Gate C2) · Starbucks: coffee, pastries, sandwiches (Post-security, Gates C7, C24) · &pizza, local quick-service pizza favorite (Post-security, Gate C28)

A Leisurely Meal

· Chef Geoff’s: Burgers and American fare from a local favorite (Post-security, Gate C14). American Tap Room: cold beers and bar food (Post-security, Gate C22) · The Chef’s Table by Wolfgang Puck:Appetizers, sandwiches, and pizza from a celeb chef (Post-security, Gate C3).

**Concourse D**  
A Quick Meal

· Dulles Gourmet Market: this food vendor has added seating, as well as beer and wine to its catalog (Post-security, Gate D5). · Dunkin’ Donuts: coffee, donuts, breakfast sandwiches (Post-security, Gates D5, D23). · Starbucks: coffee, pastries, sandwiches (Post-security, Gate D16). Potbelly Sandwich Works: custom sandwiches (Post-security, Gate D14)

A Leisurely Meal

· Bistro Atelier: Restaurateur Hakan Ilhan’s 135-seat French bistro offers sweet and savory crepes, burgers, sandwiches, and breakfast and brunch served all day. (Post-security, Gate D14). · DC Craft Brews: full-service restaurant specializing in sandwiches and beer (Post-security, Gate D23).· Bar Symon: Cleveland chef Michael Symon’s new American restaurant, featuring classic comfort food and drinks (Post-security, Gate D14).

Read the article [here](https://dc.eater.com/2014/11/20/7170513/dulles-airport-guide)

HOK to Design Major Expansion at Dulles International Airport, Adding More Than 2.8 Million Square Feet
=======================================================================================================

![Image 1](https://www.hok.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/IAD-Tier-2-and-Tier-3-Plan-HOK-1900x1270-1.jpg)

The expansion includes 22 international gates in Concourse Tier 2 in its first phase and a new Concourse Tier 3.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The [Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority](https://www.mwaa.com/) (MWAA) has selected HOK to design an expansion that will add more than 2.8 million square feet to Dulles International Airport in Northern Virginia, which serves the Washington, D.C., region.

“Our design will create an exceptional passenger experience while honoring Dulles’ iconic architecture,” said [**Susan Klumpp Williams**](https://www.hok.com/people/leadership/view/susan-klumpp-williams/), AIA, LEED AP, HOK’s co-CEO and managing principal of its [Washington, D.C.](https://www.hok.com/studios/washington-dc/), studio. “Working with MWAA, we’ll deliver a forward-thinking design that accommodates growth, enhances operational efficiency and creates a sustainable gateway worthy of our National Capital Region.”

The expansion will begin with the Tier 2 development, extending beyond the Tier 2 Concourse East currently under construction. The design will include a federal inspection services facility for international travelers, with flexibility to accommodate both narrow- and wide-body aircraft for domestic and international flights in future phases.

As part of the overall planning process, HOK will examine all aspects of the airport to enhance operations and elevate the passenger experience to accommodate expected passenger growth. This includes security processing, baggage handling, airline operations, gate requirements and more.

“As Dulles International Airport continues to break traveler records, it’s important for the airport to strategically plan its spaces for the future,” said Klumpp Williams. “We’re excited to create a comprehensive plan with MWAA to optimize space at Dulles and accommodates its future needs for airport staff, passengers, airlines, vendors and all other stakeholders.”

The design will prioritize both passenger well-being and sustainability through thoughtful choices in lighting, acoustics and materials that create a calming environment for all travelers. Sustainable design strategies will reduce energy consumption and long-term operational costs.

The design will celebrate travel in the National Capital Region. It will also honor the architectural significance of Dulles International Airport’s main terminal, designed by Eero Saarinen in the 1960s, while positioning the airport for future growth and innovation.

“Early in my career, I led the design of the main terminal expansion at Dulles and developed a tremendous amount of respect for Eero Saarinen and his work,” said [**Peter Ruggiero**](https://www.hok.com/people/leadership/view/peter-ruggiero/), AIA, HOK’s design principal. “Its design represents the golden age of aviation, and we’re honored to build on that legacy and collaborate with the MWAA to transform the airport for the future.”

The project will streamline the passenger journey by leveraging the AeroTrain system and other mobility options for efficient terminal navigation. It also will include a new central utility plant for airport infrastructure and upgrades to ramp control systems and baggage handling services.

**Customs and Immigration at Dulles International**
---------------------------------------------------

All arriving international passengers and luggage, with the exception of those arriving from pre-cleared points of origin, must be screened by [**U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP)**](http://www.cbp.gov/travel)**.** Make sure to collect all of your luggage before exiting the CBP facility; re-entry is not allowed. Passengers connecting to another flight will need to re-check their luggage and go through screening by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA). Passengers ending their journey in Washington D.C. will exit onto the Terminal Arrivals Level - Baggage Claim.

**Expedited Customs Screening Eligibility**
-------------------------------------------

Dulles has advanced technology to speed Customs screening. Click the options highlighted below in blue for more information:

*   [**Global Entry**](http://www.cbp.gov/travel/trusted-traveler-programs/global-entry) – $100 enrollment fee. Apply to CBP well in advance of travel. Approved members scan their passport and fingerprint at dedicated kiosks for expedited Customs' processing. U.S. citizens, permanent residents and citizens of a few foreign nations (see website) are eligible. Global Entry members are also eligible to participate in [**TSA Pre-check**](https://www.cbp.gov/travel/trusted-traveler-programs/global-entry/tsa-precheck) for no additional fee.
*   For passengers not eligible for these programs, simply proceed with your passport to a US Customs Officer for processing.

**Enrollment on Arrival (EoA)**
-------------------------------

Enrollment on Arrival (EoA) is CBP program that allows Global Entry applicants who are conditionally approved to complete their interviews upon arrival into the United States; including those entering the United States via a designated CBP Preclearance location. The EoA program eliminates the need for a Global Entry applicant to schedule an interview at an enrollment center to complete the application process.

When landing in an international terminal follow the signage directing you to CBP officers who can complete your Global Entry interview during your admissibility inspection. If you require assistance for your Global Entry interview because of a disability, immediately inform the interviewing CBP officer of your need for a reasonable modification or auxiliary aid or service to participate in the interview. For your planning purposes, please understand that if you use EoA and are requesting a modification, aid, or service at that time and an effective modification, aid, or service is not readily available, the interview may be scheduled for a later date.

To complete the interview via EoA, you must be in possession of the following documents:

*   A valid passport. If you travel using more than one passport, please bring them all to the interview so that the information can be added to your file. 
*   Documents providing evidence of residency. Examples are: driver's license (if the address is current), mortgage statement, rental payment statement, utility bill, etc. This is not required for minors.
*   A permanent resident card (if applicable).

**Enrollment on Departure**
---------------------------

Enrollment on Departure is available for conditionally approved Global Entry applicants departing on an international flight from Washington Dulles International Airport.  CBP's Enrollment on Departure is located in the B Concourse, across from Gate B41.  The office is open from 12 PM until 8 PM each day.

Conditionally approved applicants should arrive earlier to Dulles Airport to allow ample time to complete this interview process before their international flight departs.

In addition to the travel document, such as passport, the conditionally approved applicant will need a physical document providing evidence of residency, for example a driver's license, mortgage statement, rental payment statement, utility bill, or other document that shows a current address. This is not required for minors. Interested applicants will also need to possess an airline ticket proving their international flight.

Enrollment on Departure is not available for travelers departing Dulles Airport on domestic flights.

**Meeting International Passengers**
------------------------------------

Dulles International provides a waiting area immediately outside the International Arrivals Building in the Terminal near Baggage Claim 15  / International Arrivals. Passengers who go through U.S. Customs at the flight's country of origin will arrive through doors located between Baggage Claims 4 and 12, the same exit point as domestic flights.  More information is available on the [**Meeting Passengers**](https://www.flydulles.com/iad/meeting-passengers) page of this website.

**Contacts / For More Information**

*   [**U.S. Customs and Border Protection**](http://www.cbp.gov/)  
    **General Inquiries Hotline:** **877-227-5511** **/ CBP at Dulles:** **703-661-2800**
*   [**U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services**](http://www.uscis.gov/)
*   [**Department of State (U.S. Visa Application Process)**](http://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas.html)

### Project Overview

Solicitation Type  
Request for Information (RFI)

* * *

Issue Date  
August 22, 2023

* * *

Submission Deadline  
2:00 PM (Eastern), September 22, 2023

* * *

Online Submission  
See RFI document for instructions.

* * *

Background  
The Airports Authority utilizes a Radio Frequency ID (RFID) system to support the U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s (CBP) modified egress program at Dulles International Airport. RFID technology is leveraged for the tracking of secure document containers during the inspection process. These systems are installed within the main International Arrivals Building (IAB) Federal Inspection Service (FIS) area and within the FIS located at the Midfield (MID) Terminal. The tracking of document containers is supported by a visual/audible alarm system and is centrally managed in the command center for each FIS.

The current systems are reaching their end of serviceable life and are being considered for replacement.

* * *

Request for Information  
The Airports Authority hereby invites interested parties to respond to this RFI regarding RFID Solutions for Modified Egress that will replace/upgrade the current systems. The intention of this RFI is to better understand the current market for RFID tracking solutions within the required workspace.

The Airports Authority is seeking an RFID solution that will satisfy the CBP Modified Egress program requirements for the tracking of secured document containers during their inspection process. This includes antenna systems to triangulate the location of secure containers, visual/audible alarms should the containers enter a prohibited area, mapping software to identify real-time locations of containers, and reporting capability to show historical location data.

The Airports Authority desires to utilize to the maximum extent possible the current tags, containers, and antenna system.

Designated parking spaces are available for the disabled in vehicles displaying a government-issued plate or placard for use by the disabled. Other vehicles using these spaces are subject to ticketing and towing. Spaces have been designated in the Airport's public parking facilities:

*   [Terminal Lot](https://maps.flydulles.com/?navTo=7ff21647-055a-413d-90fc-8275c5625ab3) - In Rows 6 through 29 at the end of the row closest to the Terminal.
*   [Garage 1](https://maps.flydulles.com/?navTo=023a5615-c812-4c90-af1b-bf06d44f8353) - On Level 1 closest to the walkway to the Terminal and convenient to the shuttle stop.
*   [Garage 2](https://maps.flydulles.com/?navTo=023a5615-c812-4c90-af1b-bf06d44f8353) - On Level 3 closest to the walkway and on Level 1 convenient to the shuttle stop.
*   [Economy Parking](https://maps.flydulles.com/?navTo=023a5615-c812-4c90-af1b-bf06d44f8353) - Located throughout the lot convenient to all shuttle stops.

Parking in spaces established for the disabled are authorized for all vehicles which display a government-issued plate or placard for this purpose.  Other vehicles using these spaces are subject to ticketing and towing.  Spaces are available on a first-come, first serve basis and may not be reserved in advance.

When a parking facility is full, a uniformed parking assistant can assist you in locating the nearest available special needs parking space. Assistants will be posted outside the entrance of the full facilities. Let the uniformed parking assistant know you need a special needs accessible space; and please show the assistant your government-issued special needs parking credential.

All airport parking shuttle buses are wheelchair accessible and free of charge to all patrons.

For further questions about available parking or to request assistance, please call [703-572-4500](tel:+17035724500).

Pre-Flight Family Shopping And Dining Guide
===========================================

1.  [](https://www.flydulles.com/)
2.  Pre-Flight Family Shopping And Dining Guide

It’s summer travel season, which means it’s also family travel season. Whether heading out on a long-overdue international flight or just taking a quick getaway to grandma’s house, a seamless, tantrum-free airport experience is what most parents are after. Thankfully, with our picky-eater-approved dining and baby-essentials shopping, passing the pre-boarding time with your little ones has never been easier.

Parents know that hungry kids can quickly turn into hangry kids. First thing’s first. Make a stop at [**D**](https://www.flydulles.com/store/dc-3-hot-dog-joint)**[C3 Hot Dogs](https://www.flydulles.com/store/dc-3-hot-dog-joint)** (Concourse B). The Plain Jane Hot Dog–just a dog and its bun for your picky eater–is an easy choice. And DC3 knows its audience. Look for Kiddie Cups of soft-serve ice cream, complete with topping favorites like Oreos, chocolate chips, and M&M strawberry sauce. **[Wendy’s](https://www.flydulles.com/store/wendys)** (Concourse B) is always a winner for burgers, nuggets, and Frosties. For the chicken lovers in the family, you can’t go wrong with a stop at **[Chick-fil-A](https://www.flydulles.com/store/chick-fil-gate-d)** (Concourses B and D). [**Auntie Anne’s Pretzels**](https://www.flydulles.com/store/auntie-annes) (Concourse C) and [**&pizza**](https://www.flydulles.com/store/pizza-gate-c) (Concourses B and C) are also sure to satisfy tiny diners.

If you’ve forgotten any essentials in your diaper bag, don’t worry. Our retail stores stock many baby care items that you may need. **[Capitol City Ink](https://www.flydulles.com/store/capitol-city-ink-gate-c14)** (Concourses A, C, D, Z Gates) and [**Washingtonian**](https://www.flydulles.com/store/washingtonian-gate-b38) (Concourse B and baggage claim) newsstands sell diapers and wipes, healthy snacks, and plenty of engaging distractions like plush toys, toy planes, play cards and word find magazines. If you want a kid-friendly DC souvenir, stop by [**DC Marketplace**](https://www.flydulles.com/store/dc-marketplace) (Concourse B) or [**Uniquely DC**](https://www.flydulles.com/store/uniquely-dc) (Concourse D) to browse the offerings.

**For more kid-friendly fun at the airport, try:**

*   **[Be Right Burger](https://www.flydulles.com/store/be-right-burger)** \- Go for the chicken strips; stay for the loaded tater tots. (Concourse C)
*   [**Dunkin’**](https://www.flydulles.com/store/dunkin-gate-d5) - Coffee for you, donuts for the kids. (Concourses A, D, and Z Gates)
*   **[Five Guys](https://www.flydulles.com/store/five-guys-burgers-and-fries)** \- Burgers and milkshakes are always a hit with the small set. (Concourse B)
*   [**InMotion**](https://www.flydulles.com/store/inmotion-gate-d) \- If you (gasp!) forgot your tablet for the kids, this electronics retailer could get you set up in a pinch. (Concourses C and D)
*   [**Smashburger**](https://www.flydulles.com/store/smashburger) – Chicken strips + Tots + Milkshakes = Happy Kids (Concourse A)
*   [**Vineyard Vines**](https://www.flydulles.com/store/vineyard-vines) - Scoop up some cute swimsuits or warm weather attire for your beach vacay. (Concourse B)

Your Complete Guide to the 13 Lounges at Washington Dulles (IAD) \[July 2025\]
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Last Updated

Welcome to our one-stop guide to the 13 open airport lounges at [Washington Dulles International Airport](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/).

In this guide, we'll be covering the key amenities and access options for each lounge, noting that IAD has one of the best airport lounge footprints in the world. We have included a map showing the location of each lounge.

We have also linked to reputable independent video reviews, so you can see what each lounge looks like before your visit.

Note that with the exception of the USO Lounge, all airport lounges at Dulles are located post-security.

[Buy Washington Dulles Airport Lounge Access](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/)

![Image 1: Washington Dulles Exterior Photo at Night](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/washington-dulles-1757563020.jpg)

* * *

List of All Lounges at Washington Dulles
----------------------------------------

Washington Dulles International Airport features 13 operational lounges across the Main Terminal and four concourses. Almost all lounges are located post-security and require a valid boarding pass for access.

### Main Terminal

*   Capital One Lounge - Beyond TSA PreCheck between East and West security checkpoints
    
*   USO Lounge - Opposite Baggage Claim 12 (military personnel and dependents only)
    

### Concourse A

*   Air France - KLM Lounge - Opposite Gates A20/A22
    
*   Etihad Airways Lounge (Chase Sapphire Lounge by The Club) - Adjacent to Gate A14
    
*   Virgin Atlantic Clubhouse - Next to Gate A32
    

### Concourse B

*   British Airways Galleries Lounge - Near Gate B50, access via elevator from concourse level
    
*   Lufthansa Business Lounge - Next to Gates B49/B51
    
*   Lufthansa Senator Lounge - Next to Gates B49/B51
    
*   Turkish Airlines Lounge - Near Gate B43
    

### Concourse C

*   United Club - Near Gate C7
    
*   United Club - Near Gate C17
    
*   United Polaris Lounge - Near Gate C17/C18
    

### Concourse D

*   United Club - Next to Gate D8
    

_Note: Some lounges may have restricted access hours or specific eligibility requirements. See individual lounge sections below for complete details on hours, amenities, and access requirements._

* * *

Buying Lounge Access at IAD
---------------------------

Even if you're flying in economy without frequent flyer status, you don't have to miss out on the comfort of an airport lounge. Several lounges at Washington Dulles sell single-visit passes, allowing any traveler with a valid same-day boarding pass to enter and enjoy the amenities.

Here are the lounges you can typically buy your way into:

*   **Capital One Lounge - Main Terminal:** This lounge offers paid [walk-up access](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/washington-dulles-international-airport-main-termainl-capital-one-lounge/) for any traveller, even those without a Capital One credit card. Access is currently priced at $90 per person. Simply go to the lounge entrance to purchase.
    
*   **Lufthansa Business Lounge - Concourse A:** Access can be purchased online in advance through [the official Lufthansa website](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/washington-dulles-international-airport-concourse-b-lufthansa-business-lounge/), with prices starting from US$49, or on walk-up subject to availability.
    
*   **Air France-KLM Lounge - Concourse A:** Paid access is available [online in advance](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/washington-dulles-international-airport-concourse-a-air-france-klm-lounge/) from US$50, and sometimes available at the reception desk, but dependent on capacity and not guaranteed.
    
*   **Turkish Airlines Lounge - Concourse B:** Day passes can be purchased through third-party websites [including LoungePair](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/washington-dulles-international-airport-concourse-b-turkish-airlines-lounge-washington-dc/) from US$58. Walk-up access may be available but is subject to how busy the lounge is.
    

**Important Note:** Paid access for all airline-operated lounges is subject to capacity. During peak times, they may turn away day-pass travelers to accommodate their own premium passengers and elite members. Booking in advance where possible is always recommended.

![Image 2: Glass being held up against a sky with an aeroplane flying in the background](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/unsplash-image-wkuex4sorrq-1757563088.jpg)

* * *

Main Terminal
-------------

### Capital One Lounge

*   **Location:** Main Terminal, on the Ticketing Level. It is located after TSA Pre-Check and CLEAR security checkpoints. The lounge can be accessed from the Z-Gates on the lower level through lift or escalator. [See on map](https://pointer-app.mwaacloud.com/pointr/iad).
    
*   **Hours:** Open daily from 05:30 to 21:00. Special, reduced hours may be in effect on major holidays.
    
*   **Amenities:** The [Capital One Lounge](https://capitalonetravel.com/airport-lounges/lounge/?airportId=IAD&loungeId=C1:A8D52922-4931-4D6F-849A-BD8E25ACAA4F) is known for its premium food and beverage program. Amenities include a full buffet of high-quality, individually plated hot and cold dishes; an extensive grab-and-go section with packaged sandwiches, salads, and snacks; a full-service coffee bar with barista-made drinks and draft lattes; and a bar serving local craft beers and curated cocktails. The space also offers semi-private work areas, relaxation rooms, and a nursing room. Note that this lounge does not have shower facilities.
    
*   **Access:** Access is primarily for Capital One cardholders. Holders of the Capital One Venture X and Capital One Venture X Business cards receive complimentary, unlimited access for themselves and two guests. Holders of the Capital One Venture and Capital One Spark Miles cards can enter at a discounted rate of $45 per person. All other travelers can purchase access [on walk-up](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/washington-dulles-international-airport-main-terminal-capital-one-lounge/) for US$90 per person, subject to capacity. Access is permitted only within 3 hours of a scheduled departure.
    

_Note: Capital One are changing their guest access rules, with most cards now incurring guest charges from 1 February 2026. For more information, please see the_ [Capital One website](https://www.capitalone.com/credit-cards/disclosures/airport-lounge-terms/)_._

![Image 3: Front entry to Capital One Lounge](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/c1l_iad_signage_02_03_0622-xl-1757563141.jpg)

![Image 4: Map showing location of Capital One Lounge after TSA Precheck](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/capital-one-lounge-entry-1757563193.png)

* * *

### USO Lounge

*   **Location:** Main Terminal, on the pre-security Arrivals Level. The lounge is situated directly across from Baggage Carousel 12. [See on map](https://pointer-app.mwaacloud.com/pointr/iad).
    
*   **Hours:** Open seven days a week, from 06:00 to 22:00.
    
*   **Amenities:** The USO Lounge provides a comfortable and welcoming "home away from home" for service members. Amenities are provided free of charge and include a complimentary snack and beverage bar, a spacious lounge area with comfortable seating, a TV with a movie library, free Wi-Fi, and business services like photocopying and faxing. The knowledgeable USO volunteers can also provide assistance with ground transportation and lodging.
    
*   **Access:** Access is exclusive to active duty and retired U.S. military personnel, National Guard members, reservists, and their dependents. A valid military ID is required for entry.
    

![Image 5: Location of USO Lounge Dulles Pre-Security in Baggage Area](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/uso-lounge-1757563247.png)

* * *

Concourse A
-----------

Concourse A houses almost all foreign airlines serving Dulles and the dedicated United Express regional-jet wing (gates A1A-A6F). Carriers here include Air France, Emirates, Etihad Airways, KLM, Qatar Airways, Virgin Atlantic, plus United Express operators.

### Air France - KLM Lounge

*   **Location**: Concourse A, near Gates A19-A22. [See on map](https://pointer-app.mwaacloud.com/pointr/iad).
    
*   **Hours**: Open daily from 7:30 to 21:00.
    
*   **Amenities**: Free Wi-Fi access, power outlets and USB ports, local and international newspapers on [Air France Play app](https://wwws.airfrance.fr/en/information/prepare/divertissements-wifi-presse/app-airfrance-play-presse-et-journaux-a-bord), selection of hot and cold drinks, self-service cold meals and snacks, bar, work area, relaxation area, showers, restrooms, accessible to passengers with reduced mobility.
    
*   **How to access**: You can buy a pass to this lounge [via LoungePair](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/washington-dulles-international-airport-concourse-a-air-france-klm-lounge/). You may also have access depending on your status or class of ticket when travelling with [Air France](https://wwws.airfrance.us/information/prepare/salons#monde), [Icelandair](https://www.icelandair.com/support/airports/washington-dulles-iad/) or other [Skyteam airlines](https://www.skyteam.com/en/lounges/lounge-finder). Access is also offered to those with [Priority Pass](https://www.prioritypass.com/lounges/usa/washington-dc-dulles-intl/iad6-air-france---klm-lounge) or [DragonPass](https://en.dragonpass.com.cn/lounge/338879) membership, and select [Diners Club cardholders](https://www.dinersclub.com/cardmembers/airport-lounges-details/#!United%20States/Washington/air-france-klm-lounge-1/US041), but not between the hours of 15:00 - 20:00 daily. Access may be restricted at any time of the day for these lounge members and credit card holders due to capacity constraints.
    

![Image 6: Seating Area at Air France KLM Lounge Dulles](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/air-france-dulles-1757563301.png)

![Image 7: Air France Location Map at Dulles Airport](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/air-france-location-map-1757563359.png)

* * *

### Etihad Airways Lounge (Chase Sapphire Lounge by The Club)

*   **Location:** Concourse A, near Gate A14. The lounge is easily accessible from the Concourse A AeroTrain station. [See on map](https://pointer-app.mwaacloud.com/pointr/iad).
    
*   **Hours:** Open daily from 06:00 to 22:00.
    
*   **Amenities:** This dual-branded lounge offers a premium experience with amenities that cater to both Chase and Etihad passengers. It features a two-level design with a variety of seating zones. The food offering includes both a self-service buffet with high-quality options and a digital, made-to-order menu featuring dishes like the Sapphire Burger and noodle bowls. The full-service bar serves craft cocktails, including the signature Sapphire cocktail. The lounge also provides a family room, private restrooms, a shower suite, and reflection/prayer rooms. A unique feature is the ability for some Etihad flights to board directly from the lounge.
    
*   **How to Access:**
    
    *   **Etihad Airways access:**
        
        *   Etihad Guest Platinum and Gold members receive complimentary entry to the lounge when flying on an Etihad-operated flight, even if they are booked in Economy. Platinum and Gold members may invite one guest only when they themselves are travelling in Business or First.
            
        *   Passengers in Etihad First or Business Class (including The Residence) enjoy complimentary access; First-Class travellers may bring one guest travelling on the same flight.
            
    *   **Chase Cardholders:** Cardholders of the [Chase Sapphire Reserve](https://creditcards.chase.com/rewards-credit-cards/sapphire/reserve) and J.P. Morgan Reserve cards have unlimited complimentary access via their Priority Pass membership. They may bring up to two guests free of charge.
        
    *   **Other Priority Pass Members:** [Priority Pass](https://www.prioritypass.com/lounges/usa/washington-dc-dulles-intl/iad17-chase-sapphire-lounge-by-the-club-with-etihad-airways) members whose membership comes from any card other than a Chase Sapphire Reserve (e.g., American Express Platinum, Capital One) are permitted only one (1) complimentary visit to any U.S. Chase Sapphire Lounge per calendar year. This is a network-wide benefit, not per location. Subsequent visits and all guests incur a fee (currently $75).
        

![Image 8: Map of The Etihad Lounge at Dulles Airport](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/etihad-lounge-1757563422.png)

* * *

### Virgin Atlantic Clubhouse

*   **Location**: Concourse A, in front of Gate A32. [See on map](https://pointer-app.mwaacloud.com/pointr/iad).
    
*   **Hours**: Open daily to Priority Pass members and select Diners Club cardholders from 9:00 - 14:00 & 18:00 - 22:00 daily, and from three hours before Virgin Atlantic flights for other eligible guests.
    
*   **Amenities**: Beautifully decorated with art from local artists, sweeping views of the airport, charging stations, flight information, Wi-Fi, complimentary freshly prepared meals including the famous Clubhouse Burger, complimentary drinks service with a choice of beer, wine, and spirits, shower facilities with complimentary 30-min usage on a first-come, first-served basis.
    
*   **How to access**:
    
    *   **By Cabin Class:**
        
        *   **Virgin Atlantic Upper Class** passengers may bring one guest.
            
        *   **Delta One** passengers on international flights (no guests permitted).
            
    *   **By Virgin Atlantic & Delta Elite Status:**
        
        *   **Virgin Atlantic Flying Club Gold** members may bring one guest.
            
        *   **Delta SkyMiles Diamond & Platinum Medallion** members may bring one guest.
            
        *   _(For the above, guests must be traveling internationally on Virgin Atlantic or Delta)._
            
    *   **By Partner Airline Elite Status:**
        
        *   **SkyTeam Elite Plus** members traveling on an international SkyTeam flight may bring one guest. SkyTeam airlines at IAD outside of Virgin Atlantic include Aeroméxico, Air France, Delta, KLM, Korean Air, Saudia, and Scandinavian Airlines (SAS).
            
        *   **Virgin Australia Velocity** members (Gold, Platinum, and The Beyond) traveling on Virgin Atlantic may bring one guest who is on the same flight.
            
        *   **ITA Airways Volare** members (Premium, Executive, and Executive per Sempre) traveling on Virgin Atlantic (no guests permitted). Note that this access is likely to change with ITA having left SkyTeam on 1 May 2025 and is transitioning to Star Alliance.
            
    *   **By Lounge Membership Program:**
        
        *   Access is offered to those with [Priority Pass](https://www.prioritypass.com/lounges/usa/washington-dc-dulles-intl/iad8-virgin-atlantic-clubhouse) membership, including select [Diners Club cardholders](https://www.dinersclub.com/cardmembers/airport-lounges-details.United%20States.Washington.virgin-atlantic-clubhouse-3.IAD8/), but only from 9:00 - 14:00 & 18:00 - 22:00 daily. Access outside of these hours will not be allowed, and is always subject to space and capacity.
            

For more information on Virgin Atlantic Clubhouse lounges, [you can read our complete guide](https://www.loungepair.com/guides/virgin-atlantic-clubhouse-guide). We also recommending checking the [Virgin Atlantic website](https://flywith.virginatlantic.com/pk/en/upper-class-cabin-and-seats/clubhouse-airport-lounge/washington-dc-clubhouse.html) for current access rules, which are subject to change.

![Image 9: Seating at Virgin Atlantic Clubhouse Lounge IAD](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/virgin-atlantic-clubhouse-iad-1757563483.jpg)

![Image 10: Map showing location of Virgin Atlantic Clubhouse of IAD](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/virgin-atlantic-clubhouse-1757563547.png)

* * *

Concourse B
-----------

Concourse B hosts a mix of major international and domestic carriers including American Airlines, British Airways, Delta Air Lines, Ethiopian Airlines, Lufthansa, Southwest Airlines, and Turkish Airlines.

### British Airways Galleries Lounge

*   **Location**: Concourse B, nearby Gate B50. Access from concourse level via elevator. [See on map](https://pointer-app.mwaacloud.com/pointr/iad).
    
*   **Hours**: Open daily from 14:30 - 22:30, aligning with the evening transatlantic departure bank.
    
*   **Amenities**: The British Airways Galleries Lounge is a modern and elegant space that was fully renovated in late 2024. The lounge offers a two-tiered experience. The main Galleries Lounge features a stylish design with excellent airport views, a comprehensive buffet with hot and cold dishes, and a full-service bar with premium spirits and cocktails. Amenities include a business center, showers, and complimentary Wi-Fi. For eligible passengers, there is an exclusive Concorde Dining Room, a private, restaurant-style space offering à la carte pre-flight dining.
    
*   **How to access**:
    
    *   Access to the main Galleries Lounge is available to passengers flying Business Class (Club World) on British Airways or a oneworld partner, as well as [oneworld](https://www.oneworld.com/airport-lounges?location=IAD) Sapphire and Emerald members. Access to the exclusive Concorde Dining Room is reserved for passengers flying in First Class and for oneworld Emerald members. Oneworld airlines at IAD outside of British Airways include American Airlines, Alaska Airlines, Iberia, Qatar Airways, Royal Air Maroc and Royal Jordanian.
        
    *   The lounge is also used by eligible guests flying with partner airlines such as [Aer Lingus](https://www.aerlingus.com/prepare/airport-information/airport-lounges/).
        

![Image 11: Map showing location of British Airways Lounge at IAD Dulles Airport](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/british-airways-lounge-1757563606.png)

* * *

### Lufthansa Business Lounge

*   **Location**: Concourse B, next to Gates B49/B51. [See on map](https://pointer-app.mwaacloud.com/pointr/iad).
    
*   **Hours**: Open daily from 12:00 to 22:00.
    
*   **Amenities**: The Lufthansa Business Lounge is one of two Lufthansa facilities located near Gates B49/B51 in Concourse B. This lounge is situated on the lower level, accessible via stairs or an elevator from the main reception desk. The space is functional, offering a variety of seating, work areas, and a substantial buffet with hot and cold German and international dishes, including Lufthansa's signature pretzels. A full bar, restrooms, and shower suite are available.
    
*   **How to access**:
    
    *   Purchase [access online](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/washington-dulles-international-airport-concourse-b-lufthansa-business-lounge/) or on walk-up for US$49 per person. You can be flying with any airline. Note that the ability to purchase access may be subject to capacity at any given time or day.
        
    *   You may have access depending on your status or class of ticket when travelling with [Lufthansa](https://www.lufthansa.com/us/en/lounges) or other Star Alliance airlines.
        
    *   Access is offered to those with [Priority Pass](https://www.prioritypass.com/lounges/usa/washington-dc-dulles-intl/iad14-lufthansa-business-lounge) membership, and select [Diners Club cardholders](https://www.dinersclub.com/cardmembers/airport-lounges-details.United%20States.Washington.lufthansa-business-lounge-1.IAD14/), but only from 12:00 - 15:00 & 18:00 - 22:00 daily. Access outside of these hours will not be allowed.
        
    *   All options generally allow for a maximum three hour stay.
        

[Buy Pass to Lufthansa Business Lounge](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/washington-dulles-international-airport-concourse-b-lufthansa-business-lounge/)

![Image 12: Lufthansa Business Lounge Seating Area at IAD Airport Dulles](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/iad-lufthansa-lounge-1757563659.jpg)

* * *

### Lufthansa Senator Lounge

*   **Location:** Concourse B, sharing an entrance with the Business Lounge near Gates B49/B51. The Senator Lounge is located on the **main concourse level, upstairs** from the Business Lounge. [See on map](https://pointer-app.mwaacloud.com/pointr/iad).
    
*   **Hours:** Open daily from 12:00 to 22:00, sharing the same operating hours as the co-located Business Lounge.
    
*   **Amenities:** The Senator Lounge offers a more premium environment than its Business Class counterpart. The key feature is its location on the upper level, which provides ample natural light and tarmac views, creating a brighter and more pleasant atmosphere. The food and beverage selection is generally more extensive, and the space feels more exclusive. It includes a dedicated, roped-off area for Lufthansa and SWISS First Class passengers, offering an even higher level of service.
    
*   **Access:** Access to the Senator Lounge is strictly controlled and is more restrictive than the Business Lounge. It is reserved for:
    
    *   **Star Alliance First Class** passengers.
        
    *   **Lufthansa HON Circle Members**.
        
    *   **Star Alliance Gold** members traveling on a departing Star Alliance flight.
        

The Senator lounge is not accessible to passengers with Priority Pass, DragonPass, or other third-party lounge memberships.

![Image 13: Map showing location of Lufthansa Business and Senator Lounges at IAD Dulles Airport](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/lufthansa-lounge-iad-1757563711.png)

* * *

### Turkish Airlines Lounge

*   **Location**: Concourse B, opposite Gates B42 and B44. [See on map](https://pointer-app.mwaacloud.com/pointr/iad).
    
*   **Hours**: Open daily from 07:30 to 22:15.
    
*   **Amenities**: The lounge features a unique layout, with a main buffet and seating area upon entry, and a separate, quieter section accessible via a corridor that houses a full-service bar, an indoor "zen garden," and additional seating. The lounge is celebrated for its food and beverage program, offering a wide selection of complimentary hot and cold dishes from Turkish and international cuisines. Other amenities include a shower suite, a prayer room with an ablution facility, complimentary Wi-Fi, and business services. Read our [full lounge guide](https://www.loungepair.com/guides/turkish-airlines-lounge-dulles-washington-dc-overview) for more.
    
*   **How to access**:
    
    *   **LoungePair Pass:** Purchase a flexible lounge pass via [LoungePair](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/washington-dulles-international-airport-concourse-b-turkish-airlines-lounge-washington-dc/), which offers walk-up access without a fixed time/date booking.
        
    *   **Third-Party Lounge Programs:**
        
        1.  **Lounge Memberships:** Access is granted to members of [Priority Pass](https://www.prioritypass.com/lounges/usa/washington-dc-dulles-intl/iad11-turkish-airlines-lounge-washington), [DragonPass](https://en.dragonpass.com.cn/lounge/399544), Lounge Me, and TAV Passport. Guest allowance depends on your specific membership plan.
            
        2.  **Credit Cards:** Certain premium credit cards, such as select [Diners Club](https://www.dinersclub.com/cardmembers/airport-lounges-details.United%20States.Washington.turkish-airlines-lounge-washington.IAD11/), [Mastercard](https://airport.mastercard.com/en/lounge-finder/lounge?loungecode=IAD11), [Capital One](https://capitalonetravel.com/airport-lounges/lounge/?airportId=IAD&loungeId=COL:IAD11) and [American Express](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/travel/lounges/the-platinum-card/IAD/Turkish-Airlines-Lounge-Washington-D-C--Concourse-B-4pPs59HlBj/) cards, may offer complimentary access. Check your card's benefits guide for details on access and guest policies.
            
    *   **Airline-Specific Access (Turkish Airlines & Star Alliance):**
        
        *   **Travel Class:**
            
            *   **Business Class:** Complimentary access for passengers flying on Turkish Airlines or any [Star Alliance](https://www.staralliance.com/en/) partner airline.
                
            *   **First Class:** Complimentary access for passengers flying on any Star Alliance partner airline, with one guest permitted.
                
        *   **Airline Status:**
            
            *   **Star Alliance Gold:** Members have complimentary access and may bring one guest. This applies when flying on any Star Alliance carrier.
                
            *   **Miles&Smiles Elite & Elite Plus:** Members receive complimentary access and can bring either one guest or their spouse and children under the age of 25.
                
            *   **Turkish Airlines Corporate Club (CORP):** Members are entitled to bring one guest.
                
    *   **Airline-Specific Access (one**world **Alliance):** This lounge also serves as the official departure lounge for [select oneworld member airlines](https://www.oneworld.com/airport-lounge-results?location=IAD), noting those guests have the choice of also being able to access the British Airways Galleries Lounge. Access rules for these passengers are as follows:
        
        *   **Travel Class:**
            
            *   **Business Class:** Complimentary access for passengers flying in Business Class on Qatar Airways or Royal Air Maroc.
                
            *   **First Class:** Complimentary access for passengers flying in First Class on Qatar Airways. These passengers may bring one guest.
                
        *   **Airline Status:**
            
            *   **oneworld Sapphire**: Members have complimentary access and may bring one guest. This applies when flying on Qatar Airways or Royal Air Maroc.
                
            *   **oneworld Emerald**: Members have complimentary access and may bring one guest. This applies when flying on Qatar Airways or Royal Air Maroc.
                

![Image 14: Location of Turkish Airlines Lounge IAD Airport](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/turkish-airlines-lounge-1757563762.png)

* * *

Concourse C
-----------

Concourse C is exclusively operated by United Airlines and United Express, serving as one of United's primary hubs at Dulles with both domestic and international United flights. There are two United Club lounges in Concourse C, and a United Polaris Lounge.

### United Club - Gate C7

*   **Location**: Concourse C, next to gates C7 and C9. [See on map](https://pointer-app.mwaacloud.com/pointr/iad).
    
*   **Hours**: Open daily from 05:30 to 22:00.
    
*   **Amenities**: Full-service bar, light snacks, Wi-Fi.
    
*   **How to access**: You may have access depending on your status or class of ticket when travelling with [United](https://www.united.com/ual/en/us/fly/travel/airport/united-club-and-lounges/access.html) or other [Star Alliance airlines](https://www.staralliance.com/en/lounge-finder).
    

![Image 15: Map Showing Location of United Club nearby Gates C7 and C9](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/c7-united-lounge-1757563812.png)

* * *

### United Club - Gate C17

*   **Location**: Concourse C, next to gate C17. [See on map](https://pointer-app.mwaacloud.com/pointr/iad).
    
*   **Hours**: Open daily from 05:30 to 22:00.
    
*   **Amenities**: Full-service bar, light snacks, Wi-Fi.
    
*   **How to access**: You may have access depending on your status or class of ticket when travelling with [United](https://www.united.com/ual/en/us/fly/travel/airport/united-club-and-lounges/access.html) or other [Star Alliance airlines](https://www.staralliance.com/en/lounge-finder).
    

![Image 16: Map Showing Location of United Club nearby Gate C17](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/c17-united-lounge-1757563859.png)

* * *

### United Polaris Lounge - Gate C17

*   **Location**: Concourse C, near gate C17. [See on map](https://pointer-app.mwaacloud.com/pointr/iad).
    
*   **Hours**: Open daily from 06:00 to 22:00.
    
*   **Amenities**: Extensive buffet, full-service bar, pre-flight dining, quiet suites, showers, Wi-Fi.
    
*   **How to access**: You may have access depending on your status or class of ticket when travelling with [United](https://www.united.com/ual/en/us/fly/travel/airport/united-club-and-lounges/access.html) or other [Star Alliance airlines](https://www.staralliance.com/en/lounge-finder).
    

![Image 17: Map Showing Location of United Polaris Lounge nearby Gate C17](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/c17-united-polaris-lounge-1757563905.png)

* * *

Concourse D
-----------

Concourse D is also exclusively operated by United Airlines and United Express, complementing Concourse C as part of United's extensive hub operations at Dulles. There is one United Club lounge in Concourse D.

### United Club - Gate D8

*   **Location**: Concourse D, next to gate D8. [See on map](https://pointer-app.mwaacloud.com/pointr/iad).
    
*   **Hours**: Open daily from 05:30 to 22:00.
    
*   **Amenities**: Full-service bar, light snacks, Wi-Fi.
    
*   **How to access**: You may have access depending on your status or class of ticket when travelling with [United](https://www.united.com/ual/en/us/fly/travel/airport/united-club-and-lounges/access.html) or other [Star Alliance airlines](https://www.staralliance.com/en/lounge-finder).
    

![Image 18: Map Showing Location of United Polaris Lounge nearby Gate D8](https://i.loungepair.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,width=1200,quality=85/content/d-concourse-united-lounge-map-1757563952.png)

* * *

Closed Lounges
--------------

*   United Airlines previously operated a small lounge near Gate C4. This lounge has since closed, and is no longer listed as a Club location on the United website.
    

* * *

Summing Up
----------

Whether you're looking for a place to relax and unwind before your flight, or you need to catch up on some work, our guide to the available airport lounges at Washington Dulles International Airport has got you covered.

With a variety of amenities on offer, including free Wi-Fi, charging stations, flight information, and delicious complimentary food and drinks, these lounges are the perfect place to spend some time before your next flight.

Bookmark this guide, so the next time you’re travelling through Dulles, you'll know exactly what to expect, how to get access, and what lounge you want to visit so you can make the most of your time at the airport.

Frequently asked questions
--------------------------

Does Dulles airport have lounges?Yes, Washington Dulles (IAD) has lots of airport lounges. Our guide covers the 13 airport lounges that are currently open to the general travelling public. These lounges include the [Capital One Lounge](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/washington-dulles-international-airport-main-terminal-capital-one-lounge/), Virgin Atlantic Clubhouse, [Turkish Airlines Lounge](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/washington-dulles-international-airport-concourse-b-turkish-airlines-lounge-washington-dc/), [Air France - KLM Lounge](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/washington-dulles-international-airport-concourse-a-air-france-klm-lounge/), [Lufthansa Business Lounge](https://www.loungepair.com/at/IAD/washington-dulles-international-airport-concourse-b-lufthansa-business-lounge/), British Galleries Lounge, and numerous United Club Lounges including an upmarket Polaris lounge.

Does Dulles airport have an Amex lounge?No, Washington Dulles Airport (IAD) does not have an American Express Centurion Lounge. However, given the number of American Express cardholders in the United States, we wouldn’t be surprised if one was opened at Dulles in the future.

Capital One Lounges give travelers a modern oasis to relax and recharge. Enjoy luxurious amenities like relaxation rooms, shower suites, private workspaces and chef-inspired food you can savor at the Lounge or on the go.

**What you’ll learn:**

*   You can find Capital One Lounge locations in Dallas-Fort Worth (DFW), Denver (DEN), Las Vegas (LAS), New York City (JFK), Washington, D.C. (DCA) and Washington Dulles (IAD).
    
*   Capital One Lounges offer a space to recharge with luxurious amenities that may include relaxation rooms, private workspaces, shower suites, and local food and beverage offerings.
    
*   You can also find a reimagined culinary experience in partnership with José Andrés Group in the heart of the terminal at Capital One Landing in Washington, D.C. (DCA).
    
*   Eligible Capital One Venture X cardholders and Venture X Business primary cardholders enjoy complimentary access to 1,300+ lounges worldwide, including Capital One Lounges and participating Priority PassTM lounges, after enrollment.

#### Where will Venture X take you?

For a limited time, earn 100,000 bonus miles with Venture X. Terms apply.

How to access Capital One Lounges 
----------------------------------

Eligible [Venture X](https://www.capitalone.com/credit-cards/venture-x/) cardholders and [Venture X Business](https://www.capitalone.com/small-business/credit-cards/venture-x-business/) cardholders can enjoy access to [Capital One Lounges](https://capitalonetravel.com/airport-lounges/?utm_source=lgallaboutairport). To qualify for complimentary or discounted Lounge or Landing access, card accounts must be in good standing and cardholders must present their eligible Capital One credit card.

Lounge access policies will be changing effective February 1, 2026. To learn more about lounge access policies, please visit the [Capital One Lounge and Landing and Priority Pass™ Terms & Conditions](https://www.capitalone.com/credit-cards/disclosures/airport-lounge-terms/) for additional details. You can also visit [Capital One Travel](https://capitalonetravel.com/airport-lounges/?utm_source=lgallaboutairport) for up-to-date information about Capital One Lounges.

![Image 36: A view of people enjoying the Capital One Lounge at JFK.](https://www.capitalone.com/learn-grow/more-than-money/capital-one-lounges-arriving-in-airports/)

Which airports have a Capital One Lounge or Landing location? 
--------------------------------------------------------------

Make Capital One Lounges part of your travel itinerary when you’re flying from or through:

*   **[Dallas-Fort Worth (DFW)](https://capitalonetravel.com/airport-lounges/lounge/?airportId=DFW&loungeId=C1:51A4560C-5A73-481B-B241-820539F92DAA):** Located in Terminal D near Gate D22. Open daily from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.
    
*   **[Denver (DEN)](https://capitalonetravel.com/airport-lounges/lounge/?airportId=DEN&loungeId=C1:93FADC9E-FADD-4FF3-BFC9-7A3831C10A13):** Located in Concourse A near Gate 34 on the mezzanine level. Open daily from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m.
    
*   **[Las Vegas (LAS)](https://capitalonetravel.com/airport-lounges/lounge/?airportId=LAS&loungeId=C1:DEEFDC3A-FF39-4220-8919-BA8707D6D4BC):** Located in Concourse D Atrium on the 2nd level near Gate D50. Open daily from 5 a.m. to 11 p.m.
    
*   **[New York City (JFK)](https://capitalonetravel.com/airport-lounges/lounge/?airportId=JFK&loungeId=C1:4A47AF16-AB38-45BB-AD5B-1A9CBF7FD6F0):** Located on Level 3 in Retail Hall of Terminal 4 near B Gates. Open 24 hours.
    
*   **[Washington, D.C. (DCA) Capital One Landing](https://capitalonetravel.com/airport-lounges/lounge/?airportId=DCA&loungeId=LND:12BC1CDE-1C2A-4905-898C-128DE43CD057):** At Capital One Landing, you can experience a reimagined culinary experience in partnership with José Andrés Group. Indulge in a quick bite, or sit down and enjoy elevated beverages and tapas-style plates. Located in Terminal 2 in National Hall near Concourse D. Open daily from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m.
    
*   **[Washington Dulles (IAD)](https://capitalonetravel.com/airport-lounges/lounge/?airportId=IAD&loungeId=C1:A8D52922-4931-4D6F-849A-BD8E25ACAA4F):** Located in Main Terminal after TSA PreCheck® and Clear security checkpoints. Open daily from 5:30 a.m. to 9 p.m.
    

Keep in mind that Lounge open hours are subject to change. 

Capital One Lounge amenities 
-----------------------------

Here are a few Capital One Lounge amenities you may find on your next visit.

### Food and beverage stations 

Find fresh, chef-inspired food and beverages you can enjoy at the Lounge or on the go. Here are some of the options you may be able to find:

*   **Chef-inspired small-plate bars:** Delight in delicious, health-conscious and locally sourced options with something for everyone, including vegetarians, vegans and those eating gluten- or dairy-free.
    
*   **Full-service bars:** Sip a signature cocktail or try a locally crafted “Perfect Airport Beer” you won't find anywhere but at a Capital One Lounge.
    
*   **Grab-and-go food:** Need to eat on the run? Check out the grab-and-go options, offering sustainably packaged and easy to carry beverages, sandwiches, salads, snacks and more.
    
*   **Coffee bars:** If your travels call for a caffeine boost, enjoy fresh, hot coffee, on-tap cold brew and a full-service espresso bar. 

![Image 37: A craft cocktail at a Capital One Lounge.](https://www.capitalone.com/learn-grow/more-than-money/capital-one-lounges-arriving-in-airports/)

### Working spaces

Take advantage of thoughtfully designed working spaces, outlets near every seat and high-speed Wi-Fi. Want to research a project? Listen to a podcast? You can use your downtime to be productive in a peaceful setting while you wait for your flight. 

### Relaxation rooms 

Need a quiet space to reset? Look no further than a cozy relaxation room—available at some locations. Take a break from it all with eye masks, blankets and other luxury amenities. Breathe in. Breathe out. Get some rest. Feel better.

### Shower suites

Some of the Lounges have a shower suite so you can freshen up before you take off. 

### Luggage storage 

Worried about where to put your bags? Some Lounges provide storage with plenty of room for carry-on luggage, so you can rest and relax.

![Image 38: A view of people enjoying food and beverages at the Capital One Lounge in LAS.](https://www.capitalone.com/learn-grow/more-than-money/capital-one-lounges-arriving-in-airports/)

Key takeaways: Capital One Lounges 
-----------------------------------

Capital One Lounges are designed with luxurious amenities like relaxation rooms, working spaces, regional food and curated craft cocktails. The result is a serene oasis that’s tailored to all types of travelers.

Eligible cardholders can also access more than 1,300 participating partner lounges worldwide with a complimentary Priority Pass™ membership. Keep in mind that Lounge access policies will be changing effective February 1, 2026.
